findings.title: Negative oracle accepts unrelated implementation failures
findings.observation: AssertImplementedRejection records the production call, then asserts only non-null and not exact NotImplementedException. A NullReferenceException, KeyNotFoundException, unrelated IOException, or a different implementation bug satisfies every negative case. The current TRX correctly fails at line163, but that does not make the future rejection oracle discriminating.
findings.impact: A broken Green implementation can pass the negative matrix without rejecting the named defect or identifying its affected project/artifact. This conflicts with the accepted P0 criterion-specific precise-diagnostic assertions.
findings.remediation: For every negative case, require an expected classified rejection plus stable reason and affected artifact/project. Existing InvalidDataException with stable diagnostics is sufficient; no new public exception or dependency is required. Keep positive valid controls, and ensure setup failures cannot count as expected validation rejection.

findings.title: Command-exit cases test only the first command
findings.observation: MissingRequiredCommand removes commands[0] and NonZeroCommandExit changes commands[0]. For Unit, the order is pester,nuke-test,build-tests. Thus only Pester is independently challenged in Unit; Provider challenges nuke-provider. No case demonstrates that a missing/nonzero Nuke Test or Build.Tests result independently blocks Unit, or that an absent/unparseable exitCode cannot default to success.
findings.impact: A validator that checks only the first Unit command passes the current command tests while accepting failed or unrecorded later mandatory commands. TEST-MCP-143-AC006 explicitly names Pester, Nuke Test and Build.Tests independently.
findings.remediation: Parameterize required-command rejection by lane and command name. Cover each missing command and each nonzero exit, preserving zero exits for unaffected commands; cover missing/malformed exitCode separately. Keep later-success masking visible for earlier commands. These are validator-fixture corrections, not authorization to implement orchestration.

findings.title: Freshness and run-binding matrix does not cover all required artifact classes
findings.observation: WrongRunId mutates only selected-projects.json; stale cases mutate inventory and the first selected-project TRX. There is no stale explicit Build.Tests TRX, stale Pester XML/native-result pair, wrong-run source manifest, or wrong-run command-results case. The Pester fixtures contain counters only and do not exercise an exact-run freshness proof. Positive controls show potential acceptance but cannot prove these invalid inputs are rejected.
findings.impact: Minimal code that validates freshness/runId only where current fixtures mutate it could accept unrelated or historical mandatory artifacts. Those classes are part of this proposed report-validator boundary, not merely future producer behavior.
findings.remediation: Add independent physical-artifact mutations for stale Build.Tests and Pester evidence and mismatched source-manifest/command-results run identity, with valid companion artifacts and precise rejection reasons. Define and test Pester freshness binding using supported artifact/provenance fields or another explicit verified contract; do not invent an XSD requirement. Keep producer emission and orchestration outside this corrective checkpoint.

findings.title: Project/report mismatch is confounded with a missing file
findings.observation: ProjectReportMismatch changes reportPath to unit-or-provider/Wrong.Tests/Wrong.Tests.trx but never creates that file. A validator checking only File.Exists therefore satisfies this purported identity rejection. It does not establish that a present valid report bound to the wrong project/path is rejected.
findings.impact: The matrix can falsely claim project/report identity validation while only proving missing-artifact rejection, already covered by MissingProjectReport.
findings.remediation: Create a well-formed, existing but incorrectly bound report without introducing missing/duplicate-report confounders, and assert the exact project/path identity rejection. For example move the affected report and update its inventory path while preserving report count and content. Keep independent missing and duplicate cases.

findings.title: Source-exclusion fixtures do not exercise the actual nested candidate root

Current source drift and report-only controls therefore do not distinguish repository-relative exclusions from an absolute-path .mcpServer substring exclusion.
findings.impact: A source enumerator can pass these fixtures but exclude the entire real candidate or reject otherwise valid candidate evidence. This is a missing regression before source-enumeration Green, not a claim that the current throwing shell already implements the defect.
findings.remediation: Add a GUID-owned fixture whose repository lives under an ancestor named .mcpServer. Prove valid acceptance, edited/added/deleted included-source rejection, and report-only non-drift within that same root. Continue resolving exclusions against repository-relative paths and keep cleanup confined to the owned parent.

criteria.text: The gate validates fresh reports against run start plus source-file and tool-version manifests and rejects missing or duplicate project reports, stale reports, zero discovery or total zero, executed less than total, failures, skipped or notExecuted results, and Pester failed blocks or containers.
